claims.text: Machine-learning models would be developed and trained on existing experimental and computational data.
The proposed approach is applicable to high-entropy alloys with varying compositions.
The proposed approach is applicable across a wide temperature range.
Interactions among constituent elements affect high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic properties.
Machine-learning models can learn patterns and relationships in the available thermodynamic data.
Learning these patterns enables accurate prediction of thermodynamic properties.
The intervention would improve predictive accuracy relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention would increase the availability of melting and liquid-state thermodynamic-property estimates relative to current methods.
The intervention would improve the efficiency of determining melting and liquid-state thermodynamic properties relative to current methods.
The predicted properties include melting temperature, enthalpy of fusion, entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties.
Model performance may be limited by training-data quality and quantity.
Biases in the machine-learning models may limit performance.
